metas.name: Arizona
metas.note: Very common Arizona bollard. No surrounding states use it
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: California
metas.note: Very common bollard in California and many unique variations. When there are three letters it's the abbreviation of the county
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: Colorado
metas.note: Green flat bollards are very common and unique to Colorado. They come with 1-3 white or yellow (red is rare) reflector squares. Colorado also uses the same reflector circles as New Mexico but the green "stem" is much more common in Colorado.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: Default Tall Flat Guardrail Bollards
metas.note: Mostly found in West Virginia, Mississippi and Texas.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: Diamond Reflector
metas.note: Diamond Reflectors are used by many states but most notably Montana and South Dakota. North Dakota and Minnesota only use them on highways. If you see them in the east you're probably in Connecticut or New York
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: Guardrail Square
metas.note: This flat guardrail square is used a lot in Virginia, Maryland, Ohio, and Florida. Also found in Wisconsin, Minnesota, Nebraska, North and South Dakota but these states don't use a lot of guardrails so they will be rarer there.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: Idaho & Utah Reflector
metas.note: These are very common in Idaho and Utah, when the white reflector is all the way to the top it's often Utah, and when it's not all the way to the top it's often Idaho
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: Maine
metas.note: Like half of the time, Maine uses these tall flat bollards instead of the red/green rectangles on guardrails
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: Minnesota Unique
metas.note: You'll find these before and after guardrails. Unique to Minnesota
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: Missouri
metas.note: Missouri uses these small rounded reflectors, it's the only place I've seen them
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: Nebraska
metas.note: In Nebraska, you'll find a lot of the black Wyoming bollards with a big reflector, rounded orange rectangles and small white circle reflectors. A combination of any of them should be confirmation of Nebraska
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: Nevada
metas.note: This is one is unique to Nevada and very common
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: New Mexico
metas.note: New Mexico uses a white circle reflector in turns and three stacked orange circles (with a single orange circle on its back) before/after a turn. Not unique, used a lot in Colorado
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: New York
metas.note: Few things here, the tall sticks with white and green rounded rectangles or small squares or a single diamond. This specific guardrail is also very common in NY.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: Nothing Worth Remembering / Only On Highways
metas.note: These states don't use anything useful or only use stuff on highways. Some of these states have useful guardrail bollard metas, but that's covered in different locations
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: Oregon
metas.note: Unique for Oregon and very common. The grey part at the top is what's unique
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: Pennsylvania
metas.note: Pennsylvania uses a lot of these flat white ones with a big grey reflector that's smaller at the bottom, often with a black cap. Many states use this default looking bollard on their highways only.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: Red Green Guardrail Rectangle
metas.note: Massachusetts, New Hampshire, and Maine use these on guardrails. Red at the start and green at the end. Sometimes Maine uses tall flat bollards with the same colors instead.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: Round Reflector
metas.note: These can pop up everywhere but New Mexico, Colorado, Nebraska and Wyoming use them a lot
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: Texas
metas.note: Texas is recognizable by the unique guardrail bollard with an "inflated" bottom part. Sometimes they're just flat and not unique. Texas uses a lot of reflector tape on signs and mailboxes. The flat white bollard with three orange squares is unique to Texas
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: Vermont Guardrail Diamonds
metas.note: Blue diamond at the start and green diamond at the end of guardrails
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: Washington
metas.note: The flat brown one is unique and very common, the flat white one is not unique but very common
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: White Rounded Rectangles
metas.note: These are mostly found in Michigan, New Hampshire and Rhode Island. Michigan's are longer/taller
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: Wisconsin
metas.note: These black on white bollards are unique to Wisconsin and used a lot
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: Wyoming
metas.note: Wyoming has unique black bollards with 1-3 white or orange reflector squares. There's one version with one big reflector which is also used a lot in Nebraska. Then there's the white circle reflector with a painted top of the pole which is unique to Wyoming
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.
